practice1.prompt: Parse '{"name": "Alice", "age": 25}' into a variable called data and print the name and the age, then turn {"name": "Bob", "age": 30} back into a JSON string and print it.

cases.name: prints the parsed values and then the JSON string

hiddenCases.name: data is a dictionary you can look a key up in
the age survived as a number, not as text
both directions go through the json module
hiddenCases.describe: json.loads to read the string and json.dumps to write one

practice1.hint: One of these two functions takes a string and one takes an open file. If Python complains that a str has no attribute 'read', you reached for the file one.

questions.prompt: You have a JSON string in a variable. Which function turns it into a Python dictionary?
questions.explain: The s stands for string. load and dump work on an open file; loads and dumps work on a string in memory.

questions.prompt: A JSON file contains `true`. What does json.loads give you for it?
choices: An error, because Python spells it True
questions.explain: The module translates between the two spellings in both directions. You never write JSON's true or null in Python yourself.

questions.prompt: Match each JSON type to what Python turns it into.
questions.explain: The two structured types are the ones that matter: an object becomes a dict and an array becomes a list, so nested JSON becomes nested dicts and lists.

questions.prompt: To write a Python dictionary straight into an open file as JSON, call `json.___(data, file)`.
questions.explain: dump writes to the file for you. dumps would hand you back a string that you then still have to write yourself.

questions.prompt: Which of these are valid JSON values?
questions.explain: JSON strings are always in double quotes. Single quotes are Python, and a JSON parser rejects them.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Say why a format that is just text gets used between programs written in different languages, and name a couple of the types it carries.

reflection-exercise2.hint: The difference is what each one is handed. Say what that is for both, and the everyday situation each fits.
